correctness.rationale: Exact generating-function marking and telescoping covariance identity independently match complete enumeration through n=14. The cut-bit monotonicity proves all-n strict sign. A simple dominant root on a fixed circle gives uniform mean and probability estimates in the central window, and disjoint-block lower-tail plus local singleton influence upper-tail estimates make total discarded covariance o(1). Periodization and the Gamma integral establish the explicit profiles. All-n proof is analytic, not an extrapolation from finite experiments.

value.rationale: The number of singleton parts is an extensive statistic and the longest part is an extreme logarithmic statistic. Their correlation becomes small, yet covariance diverges logarithmically with a real digital modulation and bounded correction. Identifying the exact dependence scale and coefficient distinguishes a natural random-composition statistic from the previously studied total-part count and permits quantitative calibration of run diagnostics; it is not a routine table recomputation.
